subject: Logic
title: The Strawman
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Strawman usable.

hook.text: "So you think we should let criminals run free?" Nobody said that—but now you're defending it.

buildup.text: A strawman replaces someone's real argument with a weaker, distorted version—then attacks the fake.

discovery.text: "I want shorter meetings." "Oh, you don't value teamwork?" The original point was completely changed.

twist.text: Strawmen work because the audience often doesn't remember what was originally said.

climax.text: Counter it by restating your actual position. "That's not what I said. Here's my real argument."

punchline.text: Attack what they said, not what you wish they said.

quiz.question: What does a strawman fallacy do?
options: Distorts the argument to make it easier to attack
